summary:
--- PART 1/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "Given the tournament, the population seems to be all conditional cooperators. They will retaliate if we defect. So we should not defect except last round."
STRATEGY: Parent is a 100-round IPD strategy; trace simulates TFT-like, forgiving, probing, and endgame-exploiting opponents; it plans a TFT-with-forgiveness plus last-round defection, with no change to the given general cooperation advice.

--- PART 2/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The general advice says: \"Preserve established mutual cooperation when the partner continues cooperating.\" and \"Give a partner opportunities to return to a mutually cooperative interaction.\""
STRATEGY: Parent is a retaliatory conditional cooperator (TFT-like with forgiveness and endgame defection). The trace simulates candidate strategies against population slots (TFT, ALLD, GTFT, slot 2/3/10 probes) and revises toward forgiving probes, retaliating against repeated defection, and defecting only on the last round.

--- PART 3/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The general advice says: 'A conciliatory action can sometimes help end a chain of alternating retaliation.' So we should add: if we are in a CD cycle ... we might cooperate instead of defecting to break the cycle."
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-with-forgiveness strategy that retaliates after a defection, forgives when both defected and opponent defections are low, and defects on the final round. The trace simulates this parent against population slots (slot 2, slot 3, slot 10, slot 11, ALLD) and designs a hybrid rule: retaliate only if my_def == 0, otherwise forgive if opponent cooperation rate > 0.5. It changes the strategy to retaliate once on the first probe, then forgive subsequent probes, and keeps the endgame defection.

--- PART 4/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The general advice says to preserve mutual cooperation. So cooperating when opponent cooperates is good."
STRATEGY: Parent is a hybrid strategy: cooperate by default, retaliate on the first opponent defection, then forgive if opponent cooperation rate exceeds 0.5, and defect on the final round. Simulated against TFT-like strategies, probing strategies (slots 2,3,8,9), endgame-defector slot 10, and always-cooperate slot 11. Changed by finalizing the rule set and code, keeping only last-round defection rather than earlier endgame defection.
